description: This topic explains scalar and vector quantities, how to represent and add vectors, finding resultants, resolving vectors into components, relative velocity, and real-life applications of vectors.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
mcq.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Mass, temperature and time have only magnitude, so they are scalars.

mcq.questionText: A scalar quantity is one that has:
mcq.explanation: A scalar quantity is fully described by its magnitude (size) alone, with no direction needed. Examples include mass, time and energy.

mcq.questionText: When a vector is drawn as an arrow, the length of the arrow represents the:
mcq.explanation: In a scale drawing, the length of the arrow (drawn to scale) shows the magnitude, while the arrowhead shows the direction of the vector.

mcq.questionText: Two forces of 3 N and 4 N act at right angles to each other on a point. What is the magnitude of their resultant?
mcq.explanation: For perpendicular vectors, R = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5 N.

mcq.questionText: The law used to add two vectors that act along the two sides of a parallelogram drawn from a common point is the:
mcq.explanation: The parallelogram law of vectors states that if two vectors are represented by the adjacent sides of a parallelogram, their resultant is the diagonal drawn from the common point.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
mcq.explanation: Speed has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Displacement, acceleration and force all have direction as well, so they are vectors.

mcq.questionText: Two forces of 6 N and 6 N act in the same direction on a body. The magnitude of their resultant is:
mcq.explanation: When vectors act in the same direction, the resultant is the simple sum of their magnitudes: 6 N + 6 N = 12 N.

mcq.questionText: Two forces of 10 N and 4 N act in opposite directions on the same point. The resultant force is:
mcq.explanation: For vectors in opposite directions, subtract: 10 N - 4 N = 6 N, acting in the direction of the larger force.

mcq.questionText: A force F acts at an angle to the horizontal. Its horizontal component is given by:
mcq.explanation: When a vector F makes angle theta with the horizontal, the horizontal component is F cos(theta) and the vertical component is F sin(theta).

mcq.questionText: A force of 20 N acts at 60 degrees to the horizontal. What is its vertical component? (sin 60 = 0.866)
mcq.explanation: The vertical component is F sin(theta) = 20 x sin 60 = 20 x 0.866 = 17.3 N.

mcq.questionText: A boat that can travel at 5 m/s in still water heads straight across a river flowing at 5 m/s. The resultant speed of the boat is about:
mcq.explanation: The boat velocity (5 m/s across) and river velocity (5 m/s along) are perpendicular, so resultant = sqrt(5^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(50) = 7.1 m/s.

mcq.questionText: The single vector that has the same effect as two or more vectors acting together is called the:
mcq.explanation: The resultant is the single vector that produces the same effect as the combination of all the individual vectors acting on a body.

mcq.questionText: Splitting a single vector into two perpendicular parts is called:
mcq.explanation: Resolution of a vector is the process of replacing one vector with two perpendicular components, usually horizontal and vertical.

mcq.questionText: A man walks 30 m east and then 40 m north. The magnitude of his displacement from the start is:
mcq.explanation: The two displacements are perpendicular, so the resultant displacement = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = sqrt(900 + 1600) = sqrt(2500) = 50 m.

mcq.questionText: Two equal forces act on a point with an angle of 180 degrees between them. Their resultant is:
mcq.explanation: Two equal forces at 180 degrees act in exactly opposite directions, so they cancel out completely, giving a resultant of zero.

fib.questionText: A quantity that has both magnitude and direction is called a _____ quantity.
fib.explanation: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction, for example velocity, force and displacement.

fib.questionText: A quantity that has magnitude only is called a _____ quantity.
fib.explanation: A scalar quantity is described by magnitude alone, for example mass, time and temperature.

fib.questionText: On an arrow representing a vector, the _____ of the arrow shows the direction of the vector.
fib.explanation: The arrowhead points in the direction of the vector, while the length of the line shows the magnitude.

fib.questionText: The single vector that replaces two or more vectors is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The resultant has the same effect as all the original vectors combined.

fib.questionText: Two forces of 8 N and 6 N act at right angles. Their resultant has a magnitude of _____ N.
The horizontal component of a force F that makes an angle theta with the horizontal is F _____ theta.
fib.explanation: The horizontal component is F cos(theta), while the vertical component is F sin(theta).

fib.questionText: The process of breaking a vector into two perpendicular parts is called _____ of a vector.
fib.explanation: Resolution splits one vector into horizontal and vertical components that together have the same effect.

fib.questionText: The velocity of one body as seen from another moving body is called _____ velocity.
fib.explanation: Relative velocity is the velocity of one object measured with respect to another object.

fib.questionText: When two vectors act in the same straight line and in the same direction, the resultant is found by _____ their magnitudes.
fib.explanation: Vectors in the same direction are simply added; vectors in opposite directions are subtracted.

fib.questionText: A car moving at 20 m/s east passes a car moving at 12 m/s east. The relative velocity of the first car with respect to the second is _____ m/s east.
fib.explanation: For motion in the same direction, relative velocity = 20 - 12 = 8 m/s east.

tf.explanation: Force has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.

tf.questionText: Speed and velocity are both vector quantities.
tf.explanation: Velocity is a vector (it has direction), but speed is a scalar because it has magnitude only.

tf.questionText: The resultant of two perpendicular vectors can be found using the Pythagoras theorem.
tf.explanation: For two perpendicular vectors, R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2), which comes from the Pythagoras theorem.

tf.questionText: When two equal forces act in opposite directions, the resultant is twice one of the forces.
tf.explanation: Equal forces in opposite directions cancel each other, giving a resultant of zero.

tf.questionText: The vertical component of a vector F at angle theta to the horizontal is F sin(theta).
tf.explanation: The vertical component is F sin(theta) and the horizontal component is F cos(theta).

tf.questionText: In a scale drawing, a longer arrow represents a vector of smaller magnitude.
tf.explanation: A longer arrow represents a larger magnitude, since the length is drawn to scale to show the size of the vector.

tf.questionText: The triangle law and the parallelogram law can both be used to find the resultant of two vectors.
tf.explanation: Both the triangle law and the parallelogram law are valid graphical methods for adding two vectors.

tf.questionText: Relative velocity can never be larger than the speed of either of the two moving objects.
tf.explanation: When two objects move toward each other, the relative velocity is the sum of their speeds, which is larger than either one alone.

tf.questionText: Distance is a scalar quantity while displacement is a vector quantity.
tf.explanation: Distance has magnitude only (scalar), while displacement has both magnitude and direction (vector).

tf.questionText: Resolving a vector means combining two vectors into one.
tf.explanation: Resolving a vector means splitting one vector into two perpendicular components. Combining vectors into one is called finding the resultant.

summary.questionText: Define a vector quantity and give one example.
summary.correctAnswer: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction, for example velocity.
summary.explanation: Vectors need direction as well as size to be fully described; common examples are force, velocity and displacement.

summary.questionText: Define a scalar quantity and give one example.
summary.correctAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only, for example mass.
summary.explanation: Scalars are fully described by their size alone; examples include time, temperature and energy.

summary.questionText: How is a vector represented in a diagram?
summary.correctAnswer: By an arrow whose length (to scale) shows the magnitude and whose arrowhead shows the direction.
summary.explanation: Scale drawings let us measure the resultant directly from the arrows.

summary.questionText: State the parallelogram law of vector addition.
summary.correctAnswer: If two vectors are represented by the adjacent sides of a parallelogram from a common point, their resultant is the diagonal from that point.
summary.explanation: This law is used to find the resultant of two vectors acting at an angle.

summary.questionText: How do you find the resultant of two perpendicular vectors by calculation?
summary.correctAnswer: Use R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2) for the magnitude and tan(theta) = B/A for the direction.
summary.explanation: Perpendicular vectors form a right-angled triangle, so Pythagoras and trigonometry give the resultant.

summary.questionText: What is meant by resolving a vector?
summary.correctAnswer: It is splitting a single vector into two perpendicular components, usually horizontal and vertical.
summary.explanation: The components are F cos(theta) horizontally and F sin(theta) vertically.

summary.questionText: Write the formulae for the horizontal and vertical components of a vector F at angle theta to the horizontal.
summary.correctAnswer: Horizontal component = F cos(theta); Vertical component = F sin(theta).
summary.explanation: These come from the right-angled triangle formed when the vector is resolved.

summary.correctAnswer: It is the velocity of one object measured with respect to another object.
summary.explanation: For objects in the same direction subtract velocities; for opposite directions add them.

summary.questionText: Give two real-life applications of vectors.
summary.correctAnswer: Navigation of boats and aircraft (accounting for wind or current) and analysing forces on structures like bridges.
summary.explanation: Vectors are widely used in navigation, engineering, sports and force analysis.

summary.questionText: State the difference between distance and displacement.
summary.correctAnswer: Distance is a scalar (total path length); displacement is a vector (straight-line change in position with direction).
summary.explanation: Distance has magnitude only while displacement also has direction.

hoq.questionText: A plane flies due north at 200 km/h. A wind blows from west to east at 50 km/h. Find the magnitude of the plane's resultant velocity. (Take sqrt(42500) = 206.2)
hoq.explanation: The plane's velocity (200 km/h north) and wind (50 km/h east) are perpendicular, so R = sqrt(200^2 + 50^2) = sqrt(40000 + 2500) = sqrt(42500) = 206.2 km/h.

hoq.questionText: A box is pulled by a rope with a force of 50 N at 30 degrees above the horizontal. What is the horizontal component of the force that moves the box along the ground? (cos 30 = 0.866)
hoq.explanation: The horizontal component = F cos(theta) = 50 x cos 30 = 50 x 0.866 = 43.3 N. This is the part of the force that drags the box forward.

hoq.questionText: Two cars approach each other head-on. Car A moves east at 25 m/s and car B moves west at 15 m/s. What is the velocity of car A relative to car B?
hoq.explanation: When two objects move in opposite directions, the relative velocity is the sum of their speeds: 25 + 15 = 40 m/s, directed east (the direction of car A's motion).
